author: Thoughty2
description:
A Soviet nuclear submarine built in a rush. What could possibly go wrong?

On 4 July 1961, K-19 suffered a catastrophic failure in its reactor cooling system while deep in the North Atlantic. With the reactor overheating and no backup cooling system installed, the crew faced the very real possibility of a nuclear meltdown. So a group of heroic sailors entered the radioactive reactor compartment and improvised a new cooling system by hand.

They succeeded in saving the submarine, but at an horrific cost. Eight men died within weeks from radiation poisoning, with another 14 dying over the following two years.

K-19 would go on to become known as the “Hiroshima” and it’s not hard to see why.
title: The Submarine That Became a Nuclear Bomb
